source_text:
Dum istaec igitur apud me tacitus euoluo, Caecilius erupit: Ego Octauio meo plurimum quantum, sed et mihi gratulor nec expecto sententiam. uicimus et ita: uel improbe usurpo uictoriam. nam ut ille mei uictor est, ita ego triumphator erroris.
itaque quod pertineat ad summam quaestionis, et de prouidentia fateor et de Deo cedo et de sectae iam nostrae sinceritate consentio. etiam nunc tamen \' aliqua consubsidunt non obstrepentia ueritati sed perfectae institutioni necessaria, de quibus crastino, quod iam sol occasui decliuis est, ut de toto congruentes promptius requiremus.
At ego, inquam, prolixius omnium nostrum uice gaudeo, quod etiam mihi Octauius uicerit, cum maxima iudicandi mihi inuidia detracta sit. nec tamen possum meritum eius uerborum laudibus repensare: testimonium et hominis et unius infirmum est: habet Dei munus eximium, a quo et inspiratus orauit et obtinuit adiutus.
Post haec laeti hilaresque discessimus, Caecilius quod crediderit, Octauius gaudere quod uicerit, ego et quod hic crediderit et hic uicerit.
thought_title: Caecilius concedes and the friends depart in joy
orientation: After Octavius's long defense, Caecilius interrupts the narrator's silent reflection to concede defeat, and the three friends agree to discuss remaining questions the next day.
pass_a_gloss: While therefore I turn these things over silently with myself, Caecilius burst out: I congratulate my Octavius as much as possible, but I also congratulate myself, and I do not wait for the verdict. We have won, and in this way: even improperly I claim the victory. For as he is the victor over me, so I am the triumpher over error. Therefore, as far as it pertains to the sum of the question, I both confess about providence and I yield about God and I agree about the sincerity of the sect, now ours. Even now, however, some things remain that do not obstruct the truth but are necessary for perfect instruction, about which tomorrow, since the sun is already sinking toward its setting, we will inquire more readily, agreeing about the whole. But I, I said, rejoice more fully in the place of all of us, because Octavius has also won for me, since the greatest envy of judging has been taken away from me. Nor yet can I repay his merit with praises of words: the testimony both of a man and of one man is weak: he has the exceptional gift of God, by whom he both prayed inspired and obtained helped. After these things we departed joyful and cheerful, Caecilius because he had believed, Octavius to rejoice because he had won, I both because this one had believed and this one had won.

choices.term: uicimus et ita: uel improbe usurpo uictoriam
choices.english: We have won, and in this way: even improperly I claim the victory
choices.why: Keeps the paradoxical force of Caecilius claiming victory in his own defeat; 'improperly' renders the concessive uel improbe without softening it.
rejected: We have won, and so I even shamelessly seize the victory
We have won, and thus I claim the victory, even wrongly

choices.english: so I am the triumpher over error
choices.why: Preserves the military triumph metaphor and the genitive of the thing triumphed over, matching the source's compactness.
rejected: so I am the conqueror of error

choices.term: de sectae iam nostrae sinceritate consentio
choices.english: I agree about the sincerity of the sect, now ours
choices.why: Keeps the word order and the force of 'iam nostrae' as a parenthetical admission that the sect is now his own.
rejected: I agree about the sincerity of our sect now
I consent to the sincerity of the sect, which is now ours

choices.term: aliqua consubsidunt non obstrepentia ueritati sed perfectae institutioni necessaria
choices.english: some things remain that do not obstruct the truth but are necessary for perfect instruction
choices.why: Renders consubsidunt as 'remain' to capture the sense of questions still settling or left over, and keeps the contrast between not obstructing truth and being necessary for instruction.
rejected: some things still linger that do not hinder the truth
some points remain that do not oppose the truth

choices.term: cum maxima iudicandi mihi inuidia detracta sit
choices.english: since the greatest envy of judging has been taken away from me
choices.why: Keeps the causal cum clause and the literal 'envy of judging' to preserve the narrator's point that he no longer bears the burden of being judge.
rejected: since the greatest burden of judgment has been removed from me
since the greatest jealousy over judging has been taken from me

choices.term: testimonium et hominis et unius infirmum est
choices.english: the testimony both of a man and of one man is weak
choices.why: Preserves the double emphasis on 'hominis' and 'unius' to show the narrator's humility about his own praise.
rejected: the testimony of a single man is weak
the witness of one human being is weak

pass_b_english: While I was turning these things over in silence, Caecilius burst out: "I congratulate my friend Octavius as much as I possibly can, and myself as well, and I do not wait for a verdict. We have won, and in this way: even shamelessly I claim the victory. For just as he is the victor over me, so I am the triumpher over error. And so, as far as the main question goes, I confess providence, I yield about God, and I agree about the sincerity of the sect, now ours. Even now, however, some things remain that do not obstruct the truth but are necessary for perfect instruction. Since the sun is already sinking toward evening, we will inquire into them more readily tomorrow, so that, being in agreement about the whole, we may inquire more promptly."

Then I said, "On behalf of all of us, I rejoice more fully that Octavius has also won for me, since the greatest envy of judging has been taken away from me. Yet I cannot repay his merit with words of praise: the testimony both of a man and of one man is weak. He has an extraordinary gift from God, by whom he was inspired to plead his case and, being helped, obtained it."
After this we parted, joyful and cheerful: Caecilius because he had believed, Octavius because he had won, and I because the one had believed and the other had won.

problems.why: Latin says he obtained (something) with help, no mention of a 'request'.

edits.old: and, being helped, obtained his request

fixed: The Latin 'et obtinuit adiutus' means 'and, being helped, obtained', with no word for 'request'; the object is implicit, so 'obtained it' is the smallest fix.

problems.quote: he was inspired to speak and, being helped, obtained it
problems.source_quote: a quo et inspiratus orauit et obtinuit adiutus
problems.why: orauit means 'prayed', not 'spoke'; 'obtained it' obscures that he obtained what he prayed for.
problems.fix: by whom he was both inspired to pray and, being helped, obtained it
problems.ruling: Source says "orauit" (prayed); translation renders "spoke", altering meaning.

edits.old: he was inspired to speak and, being helped, obtained it
edits.new: he was inspired to pray and, being helped, obtained it

fixed: Changed 'speak' to 'pray' to match source 'orauit' ('prayed'); 'obtained it' is acceptable for 'obtinuit'.

problems.quote: even improperly I claim the victory
problems.why: 'Improbe' means shamelessly/boldly, not 'improperly'; 'usurpo' is seize/claim, but 'improperly' weakens the force.
problems.fix: even shamelessly I claim the victory

problems.quote: when we are in full agreement about the whole
problems.why: 'Congruentes' means agreeing/coming together, but 'ut...congruentes' is purpose: 'so that, being in agreement about the whole, we may inquire'; English inverts the logic.
problems.fix: so that, being in agreement about the whole, we may inquire more promptly
problems.ruling: Latin purpose clause ‘ut…congruentes’ misrendered as temporal ‘when’

edits.old: even improperly I claim the victory
edits.new: even shamelessly I claim the victory

edits.old: Since the sun is already sinking toward evening, we will inquire into them more readily tomorrow, when we are in full agreement about the whole.
edits.new: Since the sun is already sinking toward evening, we will inquire into them more readily tomorrow, so that, being in agreement about the whole, we may inquire more promptly.

fixed: Restructured the purpose clause to reflect 'ut de toto congruentes promptius requiremus'.

fixed.fix: he was inspired to plead his case
fixed.note: Here 'orauit' means he argued or pleaded in the debate, not that he prayed, and the checker's 'prevailed' would clash with the 'obtained it' that follows.

dismissed.why: Latin 'congruentes' = agreeing/being in agreement, not 'inquire'; 'promptius' = more readily, not 'more promptly'
dismissed.note: The English already renders 'congruentes' ('being in agreement'), and 'promptly' versus 'readily' is a matter of style; the repeated 'inquire' is clumsy but does not change the meaning.
